answer:
## Hipótesis final (respuesta al benchmark)

**Entre 1990 y 1996 la desigualdad de riqueza DENTRO de los hombres blancos y DENTRO de las mujeres blancas BAJÓ entre quienes realmente poseían riqueza, y la caída vino por homogeneización (convergencia de la parte media/baja del reparto hacia arriba), no por divergencia de trayectorias. Bajo los datos "as-reported" (ceros como riqueza cero) la desigualdad parece EXPLOTAR al alza, pero eso es un artefacto mecánico de que la masa con riqueza ≤0 crece del 29.3%→45.2% (H) y 25.3%→44.5% (M).**

Cifras del script ejecutado (muestra **B**, riqueza>0, bloque todo-cero excluido):
- **Hombres blancos**: P90/P50 **5.68 → 3.89** (Δ −1.79; IC bootstrap 95% del cambio [−2.47, −1.04]); P90/P10 **68.2 → 51.1** [−32.1, −3.3]; P75/P25 10.8 → 7.7; CV 2.25 → 1.65; Gini **0.688 → 0.623** [−0.094, −0.038]. n 2,452 → 1,900.
- **Mujeres blancas**: P90/P50 **4.89 → 3.74** [−1.79, −0.75]; P90/P10 **84.0 → 55.3** [−45.4, −11.2]; P75/P25 12.5 → 5.7; CV 2.22 → 1.60; Gini **0.681 → 0.599** [−0.109, −0.055]. n 2,713 → 2,016.
- **Muestra A (as-reported)**: P90/P50 **H 13.79 → 37.49**, **M 12.07 → 37.59** (dirección opuesta; IC del cambio [13.4, 42.0] y [15.9, 45.6]); P90/P10 **indefinido** (P10 = 0 ambos años); CV baja (2.78→2.41; 2.66→2.33); razón de diferencia media tipo-Gini plana (H 0.792→0.797, IC [−0.014, 0.026]); share top-10% sin cambio (0.621→0.620; 0.592→0.592).
- **Panel estricto** (positivos en ambas olas): H P90/P50 5.04→3.68, Gini 0.676→0.613; M 4.49→3.58, Gini 0.666→0.589. **Winsor P99** y **exclusión de ever_jailed** reproducen la dirección (H 5.52→3.84; M 4.88→3.75). Muestra **C**: caída aún mayor (H 8.31→4.50; M 8.12→3.98).
- **Mecanismo (homogeneización)**: en el panel estricto el crecimiento mediano cae monótonamente con el rango de 1990 (OLS log-growth~rank: **−2.33**, se 0.106 H; **−3.05**, se 0.112 M; p≈0). Decil 1: mediana ×8.6 (H) y ×19.5 (M); decil 10 estancado (H Δ mediano −4,750 USD, 50.0% a la baja; M −77,000 USD, 60.1% a la baja). Pero la movilidad de rangos fue alta (Spearman W90↔W96 = 0.613 H, 0.562 M): **trayectorias individuales divergentes con reparto agregado comprimido**. En dólares el gradiente por rango es +44,158 USD (H) y −98,397 USD (M): en niveles absolutos los hombres ricos ganaron más dólares (cierre relativo), las mujeres no.
- **Descomposición masa-en-cero vs propietarios** (cambio log de P90/P50 en A): total H **+1.00** = masa-en-cero **+1.45** + propietarios **−0.45**; M **+1.13** = **+1.80** + **−0.66**. La masa-en-cero explica >100% del aumento aparente; la componente de propietarios es negativa. El P50 de A pasó de corresponder al percentil 29.3 (H)/33.1 (M) dentro de los propietarios en 1990 al 8.7/10.0 en 1996.
- **Brecha H–M (secundario)**: en B la razón M/F mediana **0.824 → 0.996** (P75 0.890→1.011; P90 0.956→1.035; media 0.935→1.037): en 1990 las mujeres con riqueza estaban por encima en la mediana (58,400 vs 48,100 USD) y en 1996 hay paridad (132,000 vs 131,500); la ventaja femenina media/baja **se cerró**. Regresión de chequeo (no causal, n=9,081, HC1): `female` −0.001 (se 0.050, ns), `female:post96` −0.028 (se 0.071, p=0.70), `ever_jailed` −1.71 (se 0.243, p<0.001).
- **ever_jailed (solo sensibilidad)**: excluirlo no cambia nada. H encarcelados (n=57): mediana B 7,100→25,400 vs 49,700→134,000 en no encarcelados; %≤0 38.6%→56.1% vs 29.2%→45.0%. Mujeres encarceladas n=12 (4 y 3 propietarios) → no interpretable.
- **Contexto**: la compresión en B no es exclusiva de blancos (black male 10.00→7.04, Gini 0.762→0.706; hipanic male 9.53→4.47, 0.735→0.640).

**Calificación central**: la dirección del cambio depende de la muestra. Con imputación de persistencia para propietarios que caen a cero, **la caída de P90/P50 y del Gini sobrevive** (H 5.68→4.62, Gini 0.688→0.658; M 4.89→4.05, 0.681→0.640) pero **la caída de P90/P10 desaparece** (H 68.2→73.3; M 84.0→82.6): el cierre en el fondo del reparto entre propietarios es la parte menos robusta.

**Limitaciones**: (i) 0 codifica muy probablemente no-respuesta (25–43% de filas blancas; 29.4% H y 32.7% M de propietarios de 1990 pasan a 0 exacto; bloque todo-cero de 1,096 filas blancas, 1,092 duplicadas); (ii) sin ID no se puede verificar el panel (asumimos fila=persona) y el bloque todo-cero se distribuye desigual por sexo (17.8% H vs 13.1% M); (iii) sin pesos muestrales: nada generaliza a la población; (iv) sin edad/educación/estado civil no se descarta composición ni ciclo de vida; (v) topcoding/redondeo mitigado con winsor P99; (vi) Gini sobre A con negativos es una razón de diferencia media no acotada, usada solo descriptivamente.

**Selección declarada**: A→B retiene 70.7%/54.8% (H) y 74.7%/55.5% (M) en 1990/1996; panel estricto 49.9%/50.3%; los propietarios que caen a ≤0 eran más pobres en 1990 (mediana 32,100 vs 58,000 H; 35,100 vs 68,260 M) y 57% estaban bajo la mediana de su grupo.

payload.hypothesis: Between 1990 and 1996 wealth inequality fell within both white men and white women who actually held wealth, driven by homogenization (convergence of the middle/lower part of the owner distribution toward the top) rather than by divergence of individual trajectories; in the as-reported sample that treats zeros as true zero wealth, measured inequality instead appears to explode, which is a mechanical artifact of the share of adults with zero-or-negative composite wealth rising from 29.3% to 45.2% among white men and 25.3% to 44.5% among white women. Among positive wealth holders (all-zero placeholder block excluded): white men P90/P50 5.68->3.89 (95% bootstrap CI of the change -2.47 to -1.04), P90/P10 68.2->51.1, P75/P25 10.8->7.7, CV 2.25->1.65, Gini 0.688->0.623 (n 2,452->1,900); white women P90/P50 4.89->3.74 (CI -1.79 to -0.75), P90/P10 84.0->55.3, P75/P25 12.5->5.7, CV 2.22->1.60, Gini 0.681->0.599 (n 2,713->2,016). Same direction in a strict both-years-positive panel (men 5.04->3.68, Gini 0.676->0.613; women 4.49->3.58, Gini 0.666->0.589), after winsorizing at P99, and excluding ever-jailed respondents. Mechanism: median wealth growth fell monotonically with 1990 wealth rank among holders who stayed positive in both waves (log-growth on rank slope -2.33 s.e. 0.106 for men, -3.05 s.e. 0.112 for women, p<1e-16), with the bottom decile multiplying wealth (median log growth 2.15 men, 2.97 women) and the top decile stagnating (men median change -4,750 USD with 50.0% declining, women -77,000 USD with 60.1% declining), while rank persistence stayed low (Spearman W1990-W1996 0.613 men, 0.562 women): individual paths diverged but the aggregate distribution compressed. The apparent rise in the as-reported sample decomposes into a mass-at-zero component of +1.45 log points (men) and +1.80 (women) versus an owner-distribution component of -0.45 and -0.66. Gender gap: among holders the male/female median wealth ratio moved from 0.824 in 1990 to 0.996 in 1996 (P75 0.890->1.011, P90 0.956->1.035), i.e. white women's median advantage at the middle closed toward parity, and a log-wealth regression (female x post-1996 + ever_jailed, n=9,081) shows no significant gender level or change term (female -0.001 s.e. 0.050; interaction -0.028 s.e. 0.071, p=0.70) but a large ever_jailed penalty (-1.71 log points). Incarceration is only a sensitivity: excluding ever-jailed respondents leaves the decline unchanged (men 5.52->3.84, women 4.88->3.75), though jailed white men had far lower wealth (median 7,100->25,400 vs 49,700->134,000) and jailed white women are too few (n=12) to analyze. Limitations: zeros almost certainly encode item non-response (29.4% of men and 32.7% of women who held wealth in 1990 show exactly 0 in 1996; a 1,096-row all-zero block is 99.6% duplicated rows), there is no respondent ID so the person-level panel cannot be verified, no sampling weights are provided so nothing is representative, and there are no age/education/marital controls to rule out life-cycle composition; under a persistence imputation for 1990 owners who fall to zero, the P90/P50 and Gini declines survive (men 5.68->4.62 and 0.688->0.658; women 4.89->4.05 and 0.681->0.640) but the P90/P10 decline disappears (men 68.2->73.3, women 84.0->82.6), so the bottom-of-the-owner-distribution compression is the least robust element.
payload.workflow: Executed analysis/wealth_inequality_1990_1996.py on data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv. (1) Built four samples per group and year: A as-reported (all white rows), B wealth>0 excluding the all-zero (1985=1990=1996=0) placeholder block, strict panel positive in both years, C zero-as-missing only where non-response evidence exists; reported n and retention by group/sex to expose selection. (2) Computed per group x year x sample: P10/P25/P50/P75/P90/P95, P90/P10, P75/P25, P90/P50, P95/P50, CV, Gini (positives only), top-10% wealth share, % with wealth <=0. (3) 1,000-replicate bootstrap percentile CIs for P90/P50, P90/P10 and Gini and for their 1996-1990 changes. (4) Decomposed A-based changes into a mass-at-zero reweighting component and an owner-distribution component using the mapping q=(p-share<=0)/(1-share<=0) with a Shapley-symmetric split. (5) Measured homogenization vs divergence via delta wealth and log growth by decile of 1990 wealth in the strict panel, regression of log growth on the 1990 rank, dollar gradient, and Spearman rank persistence. (6) Robustness: winsorizing at the group x year P99, excluding ever_jailed, and re-imputing 1996 zeros of 1990 owners with their 1990 value. (7) Secondary gender gap (male/female ratios of median, P75, P90, mean across samples and years) plus a labelled descriptive log-wealth regression female x post96 + ever_jailed; ever_jailed descriptives flagged as low power (n=57 men, n=12 women); other race groups reported as one-line context. Outputs: metrics_group_year_sample.csv, change_table.csv, bootstrap_ci.csv, bootstrap_change_ci.csv, decomposition_mass_at_zero.csv, quantile_dynamics.csv, convergence_diagnostics.csv, gender_gap.csv, ever_jailed_descriptives.csv, selection_diagnostics.csv, dispersion_index.csv, imputation_sensitivity.csv, run_log.txt.
payload.primary_result: Within-group wealth inequality among white wealth holders declined 1990->1996 for both sexes (men P90/P50 5.68->3.89, Gini 0.688->0.623; women P90/P50 4.89->3.74, Gini 0.681->0.599), driven by convergence of lower/middle holders toward the top (homogenization), while the as-reported sample including imputed zeros shows the opposite (P90/P50 13.8->37.5 men, 12.1->37.6 women), which is a mass-at-zero artifact.
